nodes.summary: Write $\pi(x)$ for the number of primes $p \le x$. For natural numbers $n$ and $L$, $L$ is the $n$-th Labos prime when $n \ge 1$, $L \ge 1$, $\pi(L) - \pi(\lfloor L/2 \rfloor) = n$, and no integer $m$ with $1 \le m < L$ satisfies $\pi(m) - \pi(\lfloor m/2 \rfloor) = n$; that is, $L$ is the least positive integer with $\pi(L) - \pi(\lfloor L/2 \rfloor) = n$.
nodes.title: Labos prime

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function. For natural numbers $R$ and $n$, $R$ is the $n$-th Ramanujan prime when $n \ge 1$, $R$ is a prime with $\pi(R) - \pi(R/2) = n$, and every prime $p$ with $\pi(p) - \pi(p/2) = n$ satisfies $p \le R$. That is, $R$ is the largest prime satisfying the Ramanujan counting condition for $n$.
nodes.title: The $n$-th Ramanujan prime

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function. For natural numbers $R$ and $n$, $R$ satisfies the Ramanujan counting condition for $n$ when $R$ is prime and $\pi(R) - \pi(R/2) = n$.
nodes.title: Primes satisfying the Ramanujan counting condition

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a set of natural numbers, $v$ a real number and $m$, $R$ natural numbers, and write $\pi_P(x)$ for the number of members of $P$ that are at most $x$. Then $R$ is the $(v, P)$-Ramanujan number of index $m$ when $P$ is an infinite set of primes, $v > 1$, and $R$ is the least natural number such that $\pi_P(x) - \pi_P(x/v) \ge m$ for every real $x \ge R$, that is, every interval $(x/v, x]$ with $x \ge R$…
nodes.title: Generalized Ramanujan numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p_k$ denote the $k$-th prime, so that $p_1 = 2$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $R$, if $R$ is the $n$-th Ramanujan prime (which entails $n \ge 1$), then $R < p_{3n}$.
nodes.title: Laishram's upper bound for Ramanujan primes

nodes.summary: For a set $P$ of natural numbers and a real number $x$, $\pi_P(x)$ is the number of members of $P$ that are at most $x$.
nodes.title: Counting members of a set up to a real bound
